newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore expects substantial increase in cars.
newsitem.headline: Singapore expects substantial increase in cars.

text.p: Tiny Singapore should be able to increase its car population from 350,000 now to 540,000 in 2010 without creating major congestion problems, Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan said on Sunday.
But he said that would require continued regulation and that "Singaporeans accept that owning a car in an urbanised city does not mean that they must drive to wherever they go".
If more use is made of public transport, even by those with a car, "we will have more scope to allow our vehicle population to grow", Mah said in a speech opening a motor show.
Despite a population of some 3 million people in an area of 648 square km (250 square miles), Singapore has avoided the massive traffic problems of many Asian countries.

Among its methods have been extensive mass transportation, a system of fees and permits to restrict access to some areas at times, and a vigorous road-building programme. It is also implementing an electronic road-pricing scheme.
Probably its best-known tool has been the certificate of entitlement (COE). Without a COE one cannot buy a car. The number of COEs is limited and their price reflects demand.

In the latest month, the COE price was at Singapore $53,360 (US$38,000) for big cars between 1,601 and 2,000 cc, and S$47,764 for smaller cars between 1,001-1,600 cc. The cost of a car itself and any other taxes and fees are additional.
